name: moist_air_density_from_pressure
doc:
Compute moist-air density from a MEASURED barometric pressure.

Uses the same moist-air physics as ``estimate_air_density_kg_m3`` but
takes the barometric pressure directly instead of deriving it from
altitude via the ISA standard atmosphere.  Prefer this function when a
measured ``Pressure`` field is available from FastF1 weather data.

**Unit warning:** ``pressure_pa`` must be in **Pascals**.  FastF1
``weather_data['Pressure']`` is in **mbar (hPa)**; multiply by 100.0
before passing here (e.g. ``pressure_mbar * 100.0``).  Passing mbar
directly (e.g. 1013 instead of 101300) underestimates density ~100×.

Args:
    pressure_pa: Absolute barometric pressure in **Pascals** (Pa).
        Realistic sea-level values are approximately 80 000–110 000 Pa.
        Values below 10 000 Pa are almost certainly mbar passed by
        mistake — this function raises ``ValueError`` in that case.
    air_temp_c: Air temperature in degrees Celsius.
    humidity_pct: Relative humidity as a percentage (0–100).

Returns:
    Moist-air density in kg/m³.

Raises:
    ValueError: If ``pressure_pa < 10000``, which almost certainly
        indicates that the caller passed mbar (e.g. FastF1 ``Pressure``)
        instead of Pa.

name: estimate_air_density_kg_m3
doc:
Estimate moist-air density from altitude, air temperature, and relative humidity.

Derives barometric pressure from the ISA standard atmosphere model, then
applies the moist-air equation.  Use ``moist_air_density_from_pressure``
instead when a measured barometric pressure is available.

Args:
    altitude_m: Altitude above mean sea level in metres.
    air_temp_c: Air temperature in degrees Celsius.
    humidity_pct: Relative humidity as a percentage (0–100).

Returns:
    Moist-air density in kg/m³.

doc:

Attributes:

    n_workers: number of worker processes (>= 1).
    threads_per_worker: intra-worker thread cap (>= 1).
    priority: OS scheduling priority label (one of ``_PRIORITIES``).

name: JobExecutionError
doc: A worker job failed; carries the failing job's identity for fail-fast surfacing.

name: _detect_physical_cores
doc: Best available physical-core count, never below 1.

name: _detect_available_mem_gb
doc: Currently-available system memory in GiB.

name: _apply_ram_cap
doc:
Lower ``n_workers`` so the run fits available RAM; never drop below 1.

Logs one info line *only when the cap actually binds* (i.e. lowers the count),
naming the before/after worker counts and the memory reason.

name: resolve_resource_plan
doc:
Resolve a utilization ``level`` into a concrete :class:`ResourcePlan`.

Args:
    level: one of ``UTILIZATION_LEVELS``.
    physical_cores: physical core count; defaults to detected cores (>= 1).
    available_mem_gb: available memory in GiB; defaults to detected free memory.
    mem_per_worker_gb: assumed per-worker memory footprint; gates the RAM cap.

The resolved plan always satisfies ``n_workers * threads_per_worker <= cores``
and ``n_workers >= 1``. A RAM ceiling may only lower ``n_workers`` (logged when it
binds). The resolved plan is logged once at info level.

Raises:
    ValueError: if ``level`` is not a known utilization level.

name: _set_os_priority
doc:
Best-effort OS scheduling priority for the current process.

Windows uses psutil priority classes; POSIX uses ``os.nice``. "normal" leaves the
process untouched. Any failure is swallowed (priority is an optimization, not a
correctness requirement).

name: init_worker
doc:
Configure the *current* process for a single worker slot.

Module-level and side-effect-only so it is usable as a ``ProcessPoolExecutor``
initializer (which must be importable/picklable). Sets the BLAS/OMP thread-cap
environment variables, then — if torch is importable — caps torch's thread pool,
then applies a best-effort OS priority. The torch import is guarded so the module
and this function work even when torch is absent.

name: _run_in_process
doc: Sequential, single-process execution. Reproduces the plain sequential path.

name: _run_in_pool
doc:
Process-pool execution with input-order result reassembly.

Results are placed at their submission index, so the returned list is in input
order regardless of completion order. ``on_complete`` is invoked in completion
order. With ``fail_fast`` the first worker error is re-raised wrapped with the
failing job's identity after the pool is torn down by the ``with`` block.

name: run_jobs
doc:
Run ``worker_fn`` over ``jobs`` according to ``plan`` and return results in input order.

Args:
    jobs: a sequence of job payloads (picklable when ``plan.n_workers > 1``).
    worker_fn: a callable ``(job) -> result`` (picklable when ``plan.n_workers > 1``).
    plan: the resolved :class:`ResourcePlan`.
    on_complete: optional ``(completed_count, total, result)`` callback, invoked in
        the parent process after each job finishes.
    fail_fast: when True, the first worker error aborts the run and is re-raised
        wrapped with the failing job's identity (the pool is torn down first).
    logger: unused override hook reserved for callers that want their own logger;
        module logging always goes through ``logging.getLogger(__name__)``.

Returns:
    A list of results in the same order as ``jobs``.

name: ScopedNullResult
doc:

name: scoped_null_2023_no_repeat_circuits
doc:

name: split_half_drivers
doc:
Deterministic even/odd driver-subset partition, sorted by car number.

Sorting by ``int(driver_num)`` (not string/insertion order) makes the split
reproducible across runs and independent of ``session.drivers``' own
(arbitrary) key order.

name: circular_boundary_drift
doc:
Nearest-boundary matching drift (metres) between two tilings' INTERIOR
boundaries (the structural ``0.0``/``lap_length_m`` endpoints always match
trivially and are excluded).

Matching method: for every interior boundary in ``a``, find its nearest
neighbor in ``b`` under CIRCULAR distance (``min(|a-b|, lap_length - |a-b|)``,
since the lap is a closed loop) and record that gap. This is a directional
(a -> nearest-in-b) nearest-neighbor match, not a symmetric optimal
assignment -- documented here since the two tilings can have different
segment/boundary counts (a G2 tiling is not sector-nested in this check, so
counts commonly differ by a couple of boundaries; a MATERIAL count
difference is itself reported as instability evidence, not hidden).

Returns ``(diffs_m, n_boundaries_a, n_boundaries_b)``.

name: split_half_boundary_drift
doc:
Derive the G2 base tiling from two DISJOINT driver-subset halves of the
same weekend's field, then report the boundary drift between them.

This tests DERIVATION STABILITY directly (does the same weekend's tiling
reproduce under a different half of the field's laps?), the substantive
proxy for cross-weekend stability given #662's scoped null (see
:func:`scoped_null_2023_no_repeat_circuits`).

name: physical_corner_runs
doc:
Contiguous-run boundaries (as ``[start, end)`` segment-index pairs) of
CORNER segments in a FINAL (post-nesting) ``seg_type_code`` array.

A sector-split corner is already TWO ADJACENT CORNER segments (split-not-
snap duplicates the straddled segment's own type on both sides of the cut
-- see ``sector_nesting.py``), so ordinary contiguous-run grouping merges
it back into ONE physical corner without any sector-line-aware special
case. NOTE (documented, not fixed -- out of scope for this gate): a corner
that straddles the start/finish line would come out as two SEPARATE runs
(tiling.py's own documented non-wrapping simplification); this does not
arise for either circuit checked here.

name: physical_corner_apex_distances
doc:
Per-physical-corner apex distance (m): the ``ref.distance_m`` station of
maximum ``abs(curvature)`` among the grid points that fall inside that
merged corner run's segment span.

name: map_corner_distance_share
doc:

degenerate non-OOF path with ``usable_train=0``. That produced a passing run with
an unusable model in the 2026-06-03 gold rerun (#358); refuse to continue rather

name: build_evidence_mode_eval_batches

Build eval batches for 8 named evidence modes with sprint-weekend routing.

Modes and their routing:
- "full":     No session override, no GP filter — all rounds.
- "fp1_only": FP1 only, no GP filter — all rounds.
- "fp1_fp2":  FP1+FP2; filtered to non-sprint + 2021 legacy-sprint rounds (they have FP2).
- "fp1_fp3":  FP1+FP3; filtered to non-sprint rounds only (normal weekends have FP3).
- "fp2_fp3":  FP2+FP3; filtered to non-sprint rounds only.
- "fp1_sq":   FP1+SQ; filtered to modern-sprint rounds only (2022+ format: FP1/SQ/S).
- "fp1_s":    FP1+S; filtered to modern-sprint rounds only.
- "sq_s":     SQ+S; filtered to modern-sprint rounds only.

NAMED_EVAL_SETS_SPRINT (fp1_sq, fp1_s, sq_s) is now live; sprint-weekend rounds are
excluded from fp1_fp2/fp1_fp3/fp2_fp3 to avoid contaminating those modes with degraded
features from missing sessions.

Returns a dict of 8 keys. Modes that produce no valid batches map to an empty tuple
and emit a warning rather than raising.

name: build_recent_history_holdout_eval_batches
doc:
Build evaluation batch subsets for four round-based holdout diagnostic modes.

Modes:
- ``same_season_recent``: only rounds where round_num <= early_season_round_threshold
  (early-season rounds where within-season history is thin).
- ``round_NN``: one key per round_num (e.g. ``round_01``, ``round_02``, ...),
  each containing only batches from that round.
- ``short_gap_holdout``: rounds where days_since_prior_race <= short_gap_threshold
  (back-to-back or triple-header rounds with compressed recovery time).
  Requires a DB with event_date data; falls back to an empty list when unavailable.
- ``season_boundary_holdout``: rounds where round_num <= season_boundary_round_threshold
  (season opener through third round, before within-season history accumulates).

The batches themselves use full evidence (all sessions available); only *which rounds*
are included differs between modes.

Args:
    module_name: Latent-power module identifier.
    manifest_path: Path to the trained module manifest (unused for batch building;
        kept for API symmetry with _run_recent_history_holdout_eval).
    eval_year: Year to evaluate.
    db_path: Path to a single SQLite DB file, or None when using db_root.
    db_root: Root directory containing per-year DB files, or None when using db_path.
    race_start_target_lap: Lap used for race-start target order handoff semantics.
    max_rounds_per_year: Optional smoke-mode cap on rounds per year.
    early_season_round_threshold: Max round_num included in same_season_recent mode.
    short_gap_threshold: Max days_since_prior_race included in short_gap_holdout mode.
    season_boundary_round_threshold: Max round_num included in season_boundary_holdout mode.

Returns:
    Dict with keys ``same_season_recent``, ``short_gap_holdout``,
    ``season_boundary_holdout``, and ``round_NN`` (one per distinct round_num).
    Modes with no matching batches map to an empty list.

    compound_normalizer: Optional strict prior normalizer for the race-power module path.
    compound_allocation: Optional event compound allocation used to map SOFT/MEDIUM/HARD

    quali_sim_compound_normalizer: Optional push-regime normalizer for the quali-sim

                     back to compound_normalizer, preserving current behaviour exactly.
                     When provided, qs_* adjusted features use this push-regime anchor

value / field_median_lap_time ("spread as % of a lap"), so dispersions

doc:
Compute every constructor-pooled feature-bucket dict.

Laps are re-keyed by constructor before aggregation. Returns a kwargs-shaped
mapping (one entry per ``_assemble_constructor_raw_fields`` bucket argument);
behaviour and feature values are identical to the previous inline computation.

name: _prepare_constructor_lap_buckets
doc:
Validate, structurally clean, split and pace-filter constructor laps.

Returns ``(structural, long_run, short_run, clean, long_super, short_super)`` or
None when there are no usable laps (caller emits the empty result). Validation
and filtering are identical to the previous inline block.

name: compute_constructor_race_features_from_laps
doc:
Compute constructor-pooled race-weekend features from raw lap evidence.

Constructor features are computed from pooled constructor laps before any
driver-level aggregates are frozen. The returned feature names match the
driver race-power module-facing schema while diagnostics retain the driver
contribution counts used to assess one-car dominated evidence.

``quali_sim_compound_normalizer`` (#380): optional push-regime normalizer for
the short-run (quali-sim) bucket; when None the short bucket falls back to
``compound_normalizer`` so behaviour is unchanged.

name: _constructor_diagnostics
doc: Per-constructor contribution/lap-count diagnostics; identical to inline.

name: _filter_structural_clean_laps
doc:
Filter to structurally clean laps only.

Structural clean lap criteria:
- valid_lap = 1
- pit_in_time and pit_out_time are NULL
- All three sector times present

name: _apply_session_best_pace_filter
doc:
Apply a session-best-relative pace gate to structurally clean laps.

The reference `session_bests` can be supplied explicitly so multiple bucket
filters share the same session benchmark.

name: _filter_clean_laps
doc:
Filter to clean laps using the default production pace gate.

This compatibility wrapper preserves the old single-threshold behavior for
callers that still expect a generic clean-lap filter.

name: _filter_super_clean_laps
doc:
Build a stricter representative-lap subset from clean laps.

Uses only fields already available on the lap rows. When richer contamination
flags are absent, falls back to a tighter pace filter than the clean-lap gate.

name: _classify_stints
doc:
Classify laps into stints and return long_run and quali_sim DataFrames.

A stint is a sequence of consecutive lap numbers within a session.
- Long run: > QUALI_SIM_MAX_LAPS laps
- Quali sim: <= QUALI_SIM_MAX_LAPS laps

Returns:
    (long_run_laps, quali_sim_laps) DataFrames

name: _compute_sector_features
doc:
Compute sector-based features per driver.

For each driver, computes:
- theoretical_best: min(S1) + min(S2) + min(S3)
- expected_time: mean(S1) + mean(S2) + mean(S3)
- variation: sqrt(var(S1) + var(S2) + var(S3))

Args:
    laps: DataFrame with sector times
    use_adjusted: If True, apply compound adjustment before computing
    compound_offsets: Optional per-compound lap offsets (SOFT, MEDIUM, HARD, etc).
                     If None and use_adjusted, uses COMPOUND_OFFSETS_PER_LAP.
    compound_normalizer: Optional strict runtime prior normalizer. When present,
                     adjusted sectors are normalized to the prior target basis.
    
Returns:
    Dict[driver_id -> (theoretical_best, expected_time, variation)]

name: _prepare_lap_totals
doc: Attach raw and compound-adjusted lap totals used by representative bundles.

name: _select_representative_rows
doc: Select representative rows with super-clean priority and clean-lap backfill.

name: _median
doc: Plain median of a non-empty list of floats (used by median-relative norm).

name: _compute_bucket_repeatability_features
doc: Summarize repeatability and compound coherence within a run bucket.

name: _split_run_buckets
doc:
Split practice laps into long-run and short-run buckets.

Normal weekends use stint classification. Sprint weekends use session-aware
buckets: FP1 + SQ for short-run pace, S for long-run pace.

name: _compute_quantile_features
doc:
Compute adjusted lap-time quantiles and a best-lap proxy per driver.

Returns:
    driver_id -> (q20, q40, q60, q80, best_proxy, clean_count, super_clean_count)

name: _compute_representative_features
doc:
Compute representative-lap summaries per driver.

Returns:
    driver_id -> (best, top3_mean, robust_spread, clean_count, super_clean_count)

name: _compute_progression
doc:
Compute FP progression: improvement from FP1 to latest session.

progression = best_fp1 - best_latest (positive = found time)

Returns:
    Dict[driver_id -> progression_seconds]

name: _median_relative
doc:
Gap-to-median encoding for a pace-LEVEL feature.

``(value - field_median) / field_median``. Lower-is-better levels keep the
raw sign (faster-than-median -> negative); higher-is-better levels flip it so
better -> negative, preserving the "lower normalized = better" convention used
downstream. Missing values map to 0.0 (median == neutral); the field median is
robust to a single parked/outlier car. A non-positive or zero-spread median
degenerates to 0.0 for everyone (no scale to express gaps).

name: _field_median_lap_time
doc:
Field median of a representative pace-LEVEL feature, used as the
TIME-magnitude unit (= the field's median lap time) for dispersions.

Returns None when there is no usable positive scale (empty/all-missing
field, or a non-finite / non-positive median). Lap times are strictly
positive, so a non-positive median means no usable lap-time scale.

name: _dispersion_relative
doc:
Time-magnitude (dispersion/spread/gap) encoding for median-relative mode.

``value / field_median_lap_time`` — "spread as a fraction of a lap". A
dispersion is a TIME magnitude, so it is normalized by the field's median
LAP TIME (never ~0), NOT by the median dispersion (which can be ~0 and
explode). This puts dispersions in the SAME units as the median-relative
pace deviations ``(t - median)/median`` (both are fractions of the median
lap time). Dispersions are left UNcentered (magnitude only). Missing or
no-scale -> 0.0 (median-neutral; the adapters' ``_missing`` indicator
carries absence).

name: _extract_raw_feature_columns
doc: Project each normalized-column source field into a per-driver raw dict.

name: _compute_normalized_columns
doc:
Compute every median-relative pace column and dispersion column.

Pace LEVELS (theoretical_best/expected/q20..q80/*_best) use the
``(value - median)/median`` gap encoding; ``clean_lap_count`` and
``fp_progression`` use the higher-is-better (sign-flipped) form. Time
MAGNITUDES (variation/spread/gap dispersions) use ``value / median_lap_time``
with each run type's own theoretical-best field median as the lap-time scale.

name: _npf_normalized_fields
doc: The median-relative normalized feature values for one driver.

name: _npf_raw_passthrough_fields
doc: Unnormalized ``*_raw`` provenance fields carried straight from the input.

name: _npf_derived_fields
doc: Bounded quantity fractions, availability flags, and sector-availability.

name: _build_normalized_feature
doc: Assemble one NormalizedPracticeFeatures from the normalized columns + input.

name: _normalize_features
doc:
Normalize all features for the field (median-relative; the sole encoding).

Pace-LEVEL features (theoretical_best, expected, q20..q80, *_best, lap_count,
fp_progression) use the robust gap-to-median encoding
``(value - field_median) / field_median`` ("% off median"). For lower-is-better
pace levels, faster-than-median -> negative, slower -> positive (ordering
preserved). For higher-is-better (``clean_lap_count``, ``fp_progression``), the
sign is flipped so better -> negative. Anchored on the median (outlier-robust: a
parked/missing car cannot stretch the scale and collapse the midfield) and
expressed in fractional units (comparable across tracks/events). Missing -> 0.0
(median == natural neutral); the adapters' ``_missing`` indicator carries the
absence (see docs/evo/pace_encoding_change.md).

TIME-MAGNITUDE features (variation/spread dispersions and the *_rep_raw_adjust_gap
time gaps) use ``value / field_median_lap_time`` ("spread as a fraction of a
lap"). Unit principle — all TIME-valued inputs share one unit = fraction of the
field's median LAP TIME, so a dispersion is normalized by the median lap time
(never ~0), NOT by the median dispersion (which can be ~0 and explode). This
keeps dispersions in the SAME units as the pace deviations. Dispersions are left
UNcentered.

Genuinely dimensionless, non-time features (``*_support_saturation``,
``*_super_clean_share``, ``*_dominant_compound_share``, ``*_stint_count_saturation``)
are bounded [0,1] data-quantity fractions, not lap times, and are NOT rescaled.
See the module doc / docs/evo/pace_encoding_change.md for the per-feature
decision rationale.

name: _allfp_best_raw
doc:
Return the all-FP min-sector pace: min of the two practice-bucket raw values.

Raw seconds, lower=faster. Returns None when both buckets are missing.
When only one bucket has data that value is returned directly.
This is the canonical source for the #420 quali-pace-anchor feature (#425).

doc: Raw (unnormalized) practice features for one driver.

name: NormalizedPracticeFeatures
doc: Normalized (0-1) practice features for one driver.

Fit per-team MAP vectors (ridge) on baseline residual targets.

Returns:
