name: compute_race_car_delta
doc: Compute car capability delta from per-team weights and race context.

name: fit_race_driver_weights
doc: Fit per-driver MAP vectors (ridge) on baseline residual targets.

name: compute_race_driver_delta
doc: Compute driver capability delta from per-driver weights and race context.

name: _history_in_age_order
doc: Return one driver's history as [age0, age1, ...], where age0 is most recent.

name: _compute_driver_form_row
doc:
Compute one driver's weighting/quality arrays and form scalar.

Returns (quality, availability, w_window, w_keep, w_decay, w,
effective_count, form_value, has_min).  ``form_value`` is ``np.nan`` and
``has_min`` is 0.0 when the min-history gate is not met.

name: compute_race_form_delta
doc:
Compute race-form latent delta and diagnostics.

Returns:
  delta: shape (n_drivers,)
  diagnostics: weighting and signal arrays for debugging/breakdown

name: apply_race_form_delta
doc: Apply race-form delta to base latent power.

name: _RaceEventDateProvider
doc:
Structural type for any object exposing race event dates.

Avoids importing DatabaseManager here (which would re-introduce a circular
import) while still type-checking the duck-typed managers and test doubles
callers pass in.

name: _parse_date
doc: Parse an event_date string to a date object. Returns None on failure.

name: compute_recency_features
doc:
Return (days_since_prior_race, season_boundary_flag, same_season_flag, early_season_round_index).

Time-safe: only uses data from rounds strictly before the current round.

Args:
    year: Season year of the current event.
    round_num: Round number of the current event (1-indexed).
    db_manager: A DatabaseManager instance with a get_race_event_date method.

Returns:
    Tuple of four floats:
    - days_since_prior_race: days between current and prior race. Sentinel 60.0 if unavailable.
    - season_boundary_flag: 1.0 if this is round 1 of the season, else 0.0.
    - same_season_flag: 1.0 if prior race is from same year, 0.0 if from prior year or none.
    - early_season_round_index: round_num / total_rounds, 0.5 if total rounds unknown.

name: SampledBacktestRaceResult
doc: Backtest result for one scored race.

name: SampledBacktestResult
doc: Aggregate sampled-runtime backtest result.

name: ScoringContractError
doc:
Raised when the strict scoring contract is violated before metric computation.

The scorer requires ``set(predicted_driver_ids) == set(actual_driver_ids)``.
``scorer_skip_reason`` is one of:
  - ``missing_scoring_target``
  - ``scorer_input_contains_non_scored_entrants``
  - ``missing_predicted_scored_entrants``
  - ``driver_id_canonicalization_failure``

name: NoSampledBacktestRacesError
doc: Raised when a sampled backtest cannot score any selected race.

name: _verify_scoring_contract
doc:
Verify the strict scoring contract before computing metrics.

Raises ``ScoringContractError`` unless
``set(prediction.driver_ids) == set(actual_results.keys())``.

name: _SampledOrderScorable
doc:
Structural type accepted by the primary final-order scorer.

``FinalOrderSampleSet`` satisfies this, as does ``_RestrictedScoringView``
produced when marginalizing out non-scored (e.g. post-qualifying DNS) drivers.

name: _RestrictedScoringView
doc:
Final-order sample set restricted to the scored (racing) drivers.

A full restricted ``FinalOrderSampleSet`` cannot be built because its
``stage_snapshots`` store only per-stage aggregates (``position_distribution``)
that cannot be truthfully re-ranked without raw per-stage ordering samples.
The primary scorer never touches ``stage_snapshots``, so this view carries
only the fields ``sampled_order_metrics`` reads.

Restricting is *exact*, not an approximation: a final order is a pure rank of
per-driver latent power (``latent_samples_to_order_samples``) with no
field-interaction term, so marginalizing a driver out of the realized samples
preserves every surviving pair's relative order bit-for-bit. Dropping his
column and dense-re-ranking each sample to ``1..N-1`` therefore yields the
exact sub-marginal of the joint order distribution.

name: _position_distribution_from_samples
doc: Recompute the position distribution from a ``(sample_count, N)`` order array.

name: _dense_rank_positions
doc:
Dense-rank unique positions to a contiguous ``1..N`` scale (gap-closing).

``positions`` must hold unique values (enforced by ``_actual_position_vector``),
so argsort-of-argsort yields the ascending dense rank with no gaps.

name: _restrict_prediction_to_scored
doc:
Marginalize non-scored drivers out of a prediction's final-order samples.

Drops their columns from ``final_order_samples``, dense-re-ranks each sample
to ``1..K``, slices the pairwise matrix to the survivors, and recomputes the
position distribution. See ``_RestrictedScoringView`` for why this is exact.

name: _compute_entrant_restriction
doc:
Restrict a prediction to the scored (racing) drivers before final-order scoring.

Returns ``(scoring_prediction, diagnostics)``. When
``diagnostics["missing_predicted_scored_entrants"]`` is non-empty, the caller
must skip scoring — a scored entrant cannot be recovered from the prediction.

When the prediction contains non-scored weekend participants (predicted drivers
absent from the race classification, e.g. a post-qualifying DNS) and every driver
who raced *was* predicted, those drivers are marginalized out of the returned
final-order samples so the survivors can still be scored. This recovers the whole
race rather than discarding its finishing-order signal. Stage snapshots are left
to the caller's per-stage branch, which scores each stage against the intersection
of its drivers and that stage's actual ordering.

name: sampled_order_metrics
doc:
Compute ordinal metrics for sampled final race orders.

Enforces the strict scoring contract:
``set(prediction.driver_ids) == set(actual_results.keys())``.
Raises ``ScoringContractError`` if the contract is violated.
Call ``_compute_entrant_restriction`` before this function to record entrant
diagnostics for skip reporting.

name: stage_snapshot_metrics
doc:
Compute pairwise log-loss and Brier metrics for a StageSnapshot against actual ordering.

Uses the same pairwise formulas as sampled_order_metrics but scores the
StageSnapshot.pairwise_probability_matrix instead of the final-order matrix.

By default returns an empty dict if actual_results is missing any driver from
snapshot.driver_ids (graceful skip). When ``score_intersection`` is set, the
snapshot is instead scored over the drivers present in *both* the snapshot and
``actual_results`` (e.g. a post-qualifying DNS present in the stage snapshot but
absent from that stage's actual ordering). Slicing the pairwise matrix to the
intersection is exact — pairwise finish probabilities are invariant to which
other drivers are in the field. The caller handles the empty-dict case.

name: backtest_sampled_runtime
doc:
Run a sampled runtime over selected races with actual classifications.

By default (``plan`` is ``None`` or ``plan.n_workers == 1``) races are scored
sequentially in-process with the live ``runtime``/``db``/``compound_normalizer``.
When ``plan.n_workers > 1`` and the reconstruction paths (``manifest_path``,
``db_path``, ``compound_prior_root``) are supplied, races are scored in a process
pool via ``run_jobs`` — each worker rebuilds its dependencies from those paths.
A multi-worker plan WITHOUT the paths raises ``ValueError`` (no silent fallback).
The parallel path yields the same per_race/skipped partition in calendar order.

name: _assemble_backtest_result
doc:
Build diagnostics and the aggregate result, raising if no race scored.

Behavior-identical to the original driver tail: assembles the diagnostics dict,
raises ``NoSampledBacktestRacesError`` (carrying those diagnostics) when nothing
scored, then returns the aggregate ``SampledBacktestResult``.

name: _RaceOutcome
doc:
Tagged result of scoring one race: exactly one of ``result``/``skip`` is set.

``result`` carries a scored ``SampledBacktestRaceResult``; ``skip`` carries the
skip diagnostics dict (already merged with the race's ``base_diag``). Keeping the
two channels explicit lets the driver partition ``per_race``/``skipped`` in input
order without re-deriving which branch a race took.

name: _predict_with_oracle_state
_per_stage_metrics
doc:
Score each stage snapshot against its stage truth; return per-stage metrics + coverage.

Records stages scored over a reduced field (snapshot driver absent from that
stage's actual ordering) in ``stage_field_coverage``. Expected for a DNS in
race/race-start; on quali it usually signals incomplete classification data, so
keep it auditable rather than silently averaging a partial field into aggregates.
Each stage is scored against the intersection of its snapshot drivers and that
stage's actual ordering, so a driver absent from one stage (e.g. a DNS missing
from race/race-start truth) only drops that stage's metrics rather than the race.

name: _restrict_and_score
doc:
Restrict to scored entrants and score, or build a skip dict.

Returns ``(metrics, entrant_diagnostics, skip)``. On success ``metrics`` is the
scored metrics and ``skip`` is ``None``; on any skip condition ``metrics`` is
``None`` and ``skip`` carries the skip diagnostics (merged with ``base_diag``).
Skip semantics mirror the original loop body exactly.

name: _score_one_race
doc:
Score a single race, returning a tagged scored/skip outcome.

Pure with respect to module state: it reads only its arguments and the injected
``db``/``runtime``/``compound_normalizer``, and returns either a scored
``SampledBacktestRaceResult`` or a skip diagnostics dict. The skip/scoring/
diagnostics semantics are exactly those of the original per-race loop body.

name: _ScoreOneRaceJob
doc:
Picklable per-race job for the opt-in parallel path.

Carries only primitives/paths so it crosses a process boundary cleanly. The
worker rebuilds the live ``runtime``/``db``/``compound_normalizer`` from these
paths; the runtime is the single source of truth for the race-start target lap
(derived inside ``_score_one_race`` exactly as on the in-process path), so it is
not duplicated in the job.

name: _score_one_race_job
doc:
Module-level, spawn-safe worker: rebuild dependencies from paths, then score.

Reconstructs the runtime, database, and compound normalizer from the job's paths
(mirroring how ``_run_sampled_backtest_phase`` / ``_run_evidence_mode_eval`` build
them) and delegates to the pure ``_score_one_race``. No module-level mutable cache
is kept — each job rebuilds independently (a worker-local cache is a possible
future perf follow-up, intentionally not built here).

name: _score_races_sequential
doc:
Score every selected race in-process, partitioning into (per_race, skipped).

This is the default path and the behavior-preservation reference: each race is
scored with the LIVE ``runtime``/``db``/``compound_normalizer`` in calendar order.

name: _score_races_parallel
doc:
Score races via ``run_jobs``, partitioning input-ordered results.

Builds one ``_ScoreOneRaceJob`` per selected race (calendar order) and runs them
through ``run_jobs``, which returns results in input order. The partition into
(per_race, skipped) therefore matches the sequential path's ordering.

name: _make_sampled_backtest_on_complete
doc: Build an ``on_complete(done, total, result)`` callback logging ETA per race.

name: PriorBuildResult
doc:
Outcome of assembling one period's compound-prior root.

Attributes:
    prior_mode: ``"cross_season"`` — the isolated prior root holds 2018-2024 train-year
        priors only (no 2025 dir), so the compound-prior loader resolves a cross-season
        prior from those seasons. Matches the promoted gold's compound handling.
    prior_through_round: ``0`` for all cutoff periods — no 2025 round is in the prior.
        This is the value the leakage attestation uses.

name: PeriodPaths
doc: Isolated on-disk locations for one period's pipeline (never under params/gold).

name: render_period_config
doc:
Render the research-mode gold-cycle TOML for a cutoff period.

Mirrors the gold defaults (anchor on, quali_pace_gap, sigma calibration) but
runs in ``research`` mode so the in-season cutoff overrides are allowed, points the
compound prior at the per-period isolated prior root (2018-2024 only), and isolates every
output under the period work area. ``allow_same_season_compound_prior`` is ``false``:
cross-season prior throughout, leakage-safe, matches the promoted gold's handling. The
2018 committed prior omits beta_C1/beta_C2 (those compounds weren't run enough that year)
and the strict same-season loader requires them — cross-season avoids the load failure.

When ``inherit_fusion`` is True, ``emit_fusion_train_rows`` is set to ``"none"`` so the
gold cycle emits only the base module outputs without LOSO fusion-train rows — fusion is
inherited from the live gold config instead of retrained per-period. With ``inherit_fusion``
False (the default), ``"leave_one_season_out"`` is used (unchanged default behaviour).

name: extract_period_predictions_from_trained_result
doc:
Pull each eval round's position distribution from a trained comparison result.

``trained_result`` is the parsed ``sampled_runtime_comparison_*.trained.json`` (its
``per_race[]`` carry a ``prediction.position_distribution`` per round). Only the
period's ``eval_round_range`` rounds are collected; a missing round is an error (the
comparison must cover the whole period). ``prior_build`` carries the EFFECTIVE compound-
prior provenance (mode + through-round) so the orchestrator can attest leakage and record
the summary against what the prior was actually built through, not the nominal cutoff.

name: SubprocessPipeline
doc:
Real :class:`PipelinePort`: runs the per-period pipeline via subprocesses.

Used by the run script (and the G4 run). Each step shells out to ``py`` so the heavy
work runs in its own process. Unit tests do NOT use this — they mock the port.

name: _clear_period_root
doc:
Remove any stale artifacts from a prior (possibly crashed) run of this period.

Each period writes a fresh gold cycle, fusion config, and manifests into its
isolated ``root``. A leftover ``gold_cycle_*.summary.json`` (or fusion config, or
trained backtest) from an earlier run collides with the fresh one and trips
:meth:`_only`'s exactly-one contract (a crashed June run left two summaries in
``p1/reports`` and aborted the re-run). Clearing the period root up front makes the
per-period flow idempotent: re-running always starts from a clean, isolated tree.

name: _build_prior_root
doc:
Assemble the period prior root: copy only 2018-2024 train-year priors from gold.

The loader resolves a prior by ``<root>/<year>/compound_prior_summary.json``. The
period root holds ONLY the copied train-year priors (no 2025 dir), so
``allow_same_season_compound_prior=false`` (set in the config) resolves a cross-season
prior from 2019-2024 for all train years including 2018. This is leakage-safe (zero
2025 compound data) and matches the promoted gold's compound handling. The 2018
committed same-season prior omits beta_C1/beta_C2; the strict same-season loader
requires them, so cross-season is the only correct approach here.

A missing gold train-year prior fails loudly — that is a committed-artifact integrity
failure, not a numeric non-convergence, and must not be silently skipped.

name: _run_p0_live_gold_scoring
doc:
Inherit-fusion P0 branch: score the LIVE GOLD manifest directly over R1-6.

P0 under inherit mode IS the no-in-season-retrain promoted gold. No gold cycle,
fusion training, or assemble step is run — only the sampled-runtime comparison,
with BOTH ``--default-manifest`` and ``--trained-manifest`` pointing at the live
gold manifest (``self._live_gold_manifest``), restricted to the period's R1-6
via ``--race-name``. The period prior root is assembled from gold train-year priors
(2018-2024, cross-season) for consistent compound-prior handling. Results are
extracted via :func:`extract_period_predictions_from_trained_result` exactly as
P1-P3.

name: _assemble_trained_manifest_loso
doc:
Default LOSO path: run per-period static fusion then assemble the trained manifest.

Returns the path to the assembled trained manifest in the period report dir.
The gold manifest is passed as --source-manifest so the anchor is preserved.

name: _assemble_trained_manifest_inherit
doc:
Inherit-fusion path: skip per-period fusion; use LIVE gold fusion config.

Assembles the trained manifest from the period gold details + the injected live gold
fusion config (``self._live_gold_fusion_config``). The gold manifest is passed as
``--source-manifest`` so the anchor is carried into the assembled trained manifest.
Returns the path to the assembled trained manifest.

name: _run_downstream
doc:
Run fusion -> assemble trained manifest -> sampled-runtime comparison.

Returns the trained comparison result path. Everything stays under the period's
ISOLATED report dir; the comparison receives EXPLICIT period manifests. Default mode
(inherit_fusion=False) runs LOSO per-period fusion training. Inherit mode skips
training and uses the live gold fusion config. Both modes preserve the anchor via
--source-manifest. The global materialize step is deliberately NOT run.

name: _only
doc:
Return the single file matching ``pattern`` in an isolated period dir.

Each period dir holds exactly one artifact of each kind; >1 or 0 means the pipeline
diverged from its isolated-output contract, so fail loudly rather than guess.

name: attribute_method_gap
doc: Attribute one method's model-minus-winner gap for every tied winner.

name: SQLiteClassificationLoader
doc: Load an explicitly declared event set through read-only SQLite queries.

name: load
doc: Return one complete, hash-bound race classification per event.

name: PickScoreDetail
doc: Canonical scoring detail for one predicted driver position.

name: CanonicalScoreBreakdown
doc: Complete result from the canonical fantasy scoring path.

name: ScoringCalculator
doc:
Calculate fantasy scores for race predictions.

Scoring rules:
1. Position deltas: |predicted_pos - actual_pos| for each driver
2. Bingo bonuses: -1 for 1st exact match, -2 for 2nd, -3 for 3rd, etc.
3. Total score = sum(deltas) + sum(bingo_bonuses)
4. Lower score is better

name: calculate_score_breakdown
doc:
Score one non-empty set of picks through the canonical formula.

``predictions`` may contain any number of unique picks. Predicted
positions are unique integers from 1 through 10; position 30 is
reserved as ``DNF_POSITION`` for a selected driver absent from
``actual_results``. Actual positions are integers from 1 through 30;
classified positions are unique, while multiple drivers may share
the explicit DNF sentinel.

Raises:
    ValueError: If either input violates its declared shape or domain.

name: fantasy_score_from_predictions
doc:
Compute fantasy score for top N picks (1-10) against actual results.

Same formula as calculate_race_score: +1 per error spot, -1/-2/-3 for bingos.
Drivers not in actual_results are treated as DNF_POSITION.

Args:
    top10_picks: List of (driver_id, predicted_position), 1-10 items.
    actual_results: Dict driver_id -> actual finishing position (1-indexed).

Returns:
    Total fantasy score (lower is better), or None if no picks.

name: calculate_race_score
doc:
Calculate score for a set of predictions against actual results.

Args:
    predictions: List of (driver_id, predicted_position) tuples
    actual_results: List of driver_ids in actual finishing order (1st to last)

Returns:
    ScoreBreakdown with complete scoring details

Raises:
    ValueError: If predictions or actual_results are invalid

name: calculate_score_from_strategy
doc:
Calculate score for a PickStrategy against actual results.

Args:
    strategy: PickStrategy with picks
    actual_results: Actual finishing order

Returns:
    ScoreBreakdown with scoring details

name: get_score_summary
doc:
Get human-readable summary of score breakdown.

Args:
    breakdown: ScoreBreakdown to summarize

Returns:
    Multi-line string summary

name: _smoother_version
doc:
The trajectory smoother's version tag, imported lazily so this module's
import path stays free of the (FastF1-touching) ``trajectory`` package
(mirrors ``generator._build_ribbon``'s own lazy trajectory-side imports).

name: _get_session_id
doc:
``sessions.id`` for (year, gp, session_type), or None if absent/missing DB.

Guards ``Path(db_path).exists()`` first: ``sqlite3.connect`` silently
CREATES a missing file, which would otherwise leave junk empty DBs behind
for a mistyped ``data_dir``.

name: _load_session_laps
doc:
All ``lap_times`` rows (every driver) for one session_id.

Columns: driver, lap_number, compound, tyre_life, lap_time, track_status,
valid_lap, pit_in_time, pit_out_time, stint_id.

name: _load_ok_fits
doc:
Drivers with an ok Q-session fit for (year, gp) -- the car-capability
anchor ``ideal_lap`` derates. Race sessions have no fit of their own (the
v1 ceiling is Q-only, see the design doc); this is the SAME row
``ideal_lap`` would load itself via ``session_type="Q"``, fetched once
here so every clean race lap of a driver reuses the identical row instead
of re-querying FitStore per lap.

name: _build_terrain
doc:
ONE pooled terrain profile for this (year, gp) -- Task 11 (wire terrain
banking into the ideal lap). Built ONCE before the per-driver loop and
threaded into every ``gen.ideal_lap``/``gen.ideal_lap_sigma_grid`` call
this gp: banking is a circuit property, not a per-driver or per-lap one.

Pools raw per-lap XYZ position traces straight off FastF1 ``pos_data``
(any laps do -- no smoother/regime-classification needed here, mirroring
``session_coast``'s "any laps will do" per-lap XYZ collection for the
terrain centerline; unlike ``session_lateral``/``session_traction``'s
``_driver_samples``, which additionally fits+classifies each lap for
THEIR OWN kinematic samples -- machinery this builder has no use for).
``build_terrain_profile`` needs ``min_laps=3`` total laps pooled; with a
full driver field this is essentially always satisfied.

Returns ``None`` (logged once, never raised) when the session can't be
loaded or too few usable laps are found -- callers then thread
``terrain=None`` into every ``ideal_lap`` call this gp, which reproduces
the pre-Task-11 flat-track (no ``bank_rad`` column) behaviour exactly.

name: _wear_push_quantile
doc:
The ``push_quantile`` (Task 4, capability-wear-model-v2) the pinned
``wear_run_id`` was built with -- the push threshold that defines
"capability" (see ``wear.batch.run_batch``'s ``params_json``).

Read via a raw ``wear_runs.params_json`` query -- ``WearModel`` itself
excludes ``params_json`` (mirrors this module's own
``EphemerisModel``/``source_versions_json`` split). Returns ``None``
(never a crash, never a fabricated value) when ``wear_run_id`` is
``None``, ``wear_db_path`` doesn't exist, ``wear_runs`` isn't present, the
run row is missing, or the run predates capability/coast entirely (its
``params_json`` has no ``"push_quantile"`` key -- a realized-only wear
model, which correctly has no push threshold to pin).

name: _bilinear
doc:
Bilinear interpolation of ``values`` (shape ``(len(ages), len(masses))``)
at (``age``, ``mass``), CLAMPED to the grid bounds (a lap's tyre age or
fuel mass outside the grid -- e.g. a >25-lap stint -- reads the nearest
edge rather than extrapolating a Monte-Carlo sigma off the sampled grid).

name: _grid_sensitivities
doc:
``(dLap/dmass, dLap/dage)`` at (``age``, ``mass``): the bilinear partial
derivatives of the grid's deterministic nominal lap-time surface
(``grid.lap_s``) within the enclosing cell (clamped to the grid). Units:
s/kg and s/lap. Zero on a degenerate (collapsed) mass or age axis.

name: _kappa_sensitivities
doc:
``(dLap/dkappa_lat, dLap/dkappa_long)`` from the grid's total age
sensitivity ``dLdage``.

The ideal derates against the products ``kappa_lat*age`` and
``kappa_long*age``; the age-axis grid measures only the COMBINED
``dLap/dage = sum_axis (dLap/d(kappa_axis*age)) * kappa_axis``. This splits
it under an equal-marginal-sensitivity assumption
(``dLap/d(kappa_lat*age) == dLap/d(kappa_long*age)``), which reconstructs
``dLdage`` exactly and gives each ACTIVE axis
``dLap/dkappa_axis = dLdage * age / (kappa_lat_eff + kappa_long_eff)`` --
symmetric, and stable as kappa -> 0 (``dLdage`` itself vanishes with
kappa, so the ratio does not blow up). A negative kappa contributes
nothing (``kappa_eff = max(kappa, 0)``), matching the derate's own
negative-kappa clamp (a negative/track-evolution kappa is not tyre
aging). This is part of the blob's approximate-by-construction nature
(a single age axis cannot fully separate the two axes' leverage).

name: _assemble_cov
doc:
The RAW (pre-PSD-repair) 4x4 covariance over
(mass_kg, kappa_lat, kappa_long, residual_s), built by the delta method.

Input block ``Sigma_in`` (3x3 over mass/kappa_lat/kappa_long): diagonal =
the plain variances; mass x kappa off-diagonals =
``massbeta_kappa_corr_axis * mass_se * kappa_axis_se`` (Task 7's pooled
beta_mass x kappa correlation scaled by the two sigmas); kappa_lat x
kappa_long = 0 (no measured cross-axis correlation). The residual row is
the delta-method image of ``resid = observed - ideal(mass, kappa...)``:
with Jacobian ``J = [-dLdm, -dLdk_lat, -dLdk_long]``, ``cov(x_i, resid) =
(Sigma_in @ J)_i`` and ``var(resid) = J @ Sigma_in @ J + sigma_ceiling**2``
(the ceiling-covariance MC term is an INDEPENDENT additive source).

``Sigma_in`` is PSD by construction, but ONLY after the joint-correlation
clamp below: each pooled correlation is individually valid in [-1, 1], yet
the mass/kappa block is PSD iff ``corr_lat**2 + corr_long**2 <= 1`` (the
det of its correlation matrix is ``1 - corr_lat**2 - corr_long**2``). When
the two pooled scalars jointly leave the unit disk they are scaled -- both
by the same factor, ratio preserved -- to land just inside it, so
``Sigma_in`` (and hence the whole 4x4, a linear map of a PSD block plus
independent ceiling noise) is genuinely PSD. ``_psd_repair`` is therefore a
LAST-RESORT numerical guard, NOT part of the construction: on this
function's output it must be a no-op (its firing would indicate a bug, e.g.
a floating-point negative eigenvalue), and crucially it never has to
silently move a diagonal away from the input variances.

``None`` sigmas/correlations (no wear model, no pooled correlation) are
treated as 0.0 -- an absent source contributes no (co)variance, never a
fabricated one.

name: _psd_repair
doc:
Eigenvalue-clip PSD repair: symmetrise, eigendecompose, clip negative
eigenvalues to 0, reconstruct. Returns a symmetric matrix whose
``eigvalsh`` are all ``>= -1e-9`` (numerical).

This is a LAST-RESORT numerical guard, not part of the construction:
``_assemble_cov`` (with its joint-correlation clamp) already returns a PSD
matrix, so on that output this is a no-op. If it EVER moves a value it is
repairing a real numerical negative eigenvalue -- and moving the diagonal
would mean the stored variances no longer equal ``mass_se**2`` etc., which
would be a bug in the assembly rather than something to paper over here.
Retained (and unit-tested in isolation) so a future non-PSD input can never
reach the store.

name: _massbeta_corr
doc:
The wear run's pooled beta_mass x kappa correlation for ``axis`` (Task
7's ``WearModel.massbeta_kappa_corr``), or ``None`` when the model carries
none (mass_beta was off, or a legacy/hand-built model without the field).
Guarded with ``getattr``/``isinstance`` so a non-``WearModel`` stub (some
offline tests pass a bare ``object()``) yields ``None``, not a crash.

name: _build_sigma_grid
doc:
``gen.ideal_lap_sigma_grid`` for one (driver, compound), reusing the
per-driver cached ribbon + power-curve-baked fit row (so the grid drives
the identical ceiling ``ideal_lap`` does) and the per-gp ``terrain``
(Task 11) -- so the grid's shared track_df carries the SAME banking every
per-lap ``ideal_lap`` call this gp uses. Returns ``None`` on ANY failure
(logged, never fatal) -- a driver/compound whose grid can't be built gets
``residual_se``/``cov_json`` left NULL rather than a fabricated value,
matching this module's per-lap "never fabricate" robustness.

name: _is_clean_lap
doc:
Clean-race-lap gate: valid_lap + no pit in/out + green flag + a real
stint id (session_race's g2 gate), PLUS the fields this builder can't
build a state/residual row without (a real lap_time, compound, tyre_life).

name: _track_statuses_for_driver
doc:
Per-lap track_status vector (index 0 = lap 1) for one driver, filling
missing laps with "1" (green) -- ``race_mass``'s hard gate never receives
``track_statuses=None``.

name: _build_gp_rows
doc:
One (year, gp)'s state/residual rows. Returns ``(state_rows,
residual_rows, engine_shas, ceiling_sources)`` -- all empty/empty
set/empty dict when the session, lap_times, or ok Q fits are absent
(never raises for that; a per-lap ``ideal_lap`` failure is also
swallowed, see module docstring). ``ceiling_sources`` is a driver ->
``IdealLapResult.ceiling_source_used`` map (Task 1) -- constant across
every lap of one driver's stint at this gp (same fit row/round_idx
throughout), so the last lap's value is representative.

name: build_ephemeris
doc:
Build one ephemeris run over ``years`` x ``gps`` (race sessions) and
write it via ``ephemeris_store.write_run``. Returns the new run_id.

``gps="all"`` resolves per-year via ``src.utils.constants.get_calendar``;
a year absent from the calendar table is logged and skipped (never
aborts the whole multi-year batch). Every (year, gp) is independently
isolated the same way -- one bad circuit's exception is logged and
skipped, mirroring ``src.physics.wear.batch``/``sweep.sweep_event``'s
per-unit robustness.

``ceiling_source``/``estimate_db_path`` (Task 1) thread straight through
to every ``gen.ideal_lap`` call, same as ``fit_db_path``/``wear_db_path``.

name: _group_by_team
doc: (driver, constructor) pairs -> {constructor: [drivers]}, order-preserving.

name: run_estimate_batch
doc:
Populate ``store`` with one cross-view estimate per (season, GP, constructor).

Loads each quali once and reuses it for every constructor + every view of that GP.
Returns counts {fitted, skipped, errors, sessions_missing, constructors}.

name: run_grip_batch
doc:
Populate ``store`` with one grip-baseline record per (season, GP, session_type).

Returns counts ``{fitted, skipped, errors, sessions_missing}``.

name: RaceStintData
doc:
One qualifying stint's worth of race telemetry, ready for g3 fitting.

All arrays are ordered by ascending lap_number (clean laps only).

Fields
------
year          : Championship year.
gp            : Circuit name matching the ``lap_times`` session (e.g. 'Bahrain').
driver        : Driver abbreviation (e.g. 'VER').
stint_num     : 1-based stint index for this driver in this race (ordered by
                the first clean lap number within the stint).
compound      : Tyre compound for this stint: SOFT / MEDIUM / HARD.
lap_nums      : Race lap numbers of clean laps in this stint. Shape: [n_clean].
tyre_life     : ABSOLUTE tyre_life per clean lap from lap_times. Shape: [n_clean].
                NOTE: VER Bahrain 2023 stint 1 starts at 4 (not 0) due to
                FastF1 installation-lap accounting. Do NOT subtract the min.
processed_df  : Smoother output for all clean laps concatenated.
                Includes a 'lap_number' column (int).
mass_kg       : Per-lap race mass (kg). Shape: [n_clean].
                mass_kg[i] = race_mass(year, gp, lap_nums[i], n_race_laps,
                                       track_statuses=all_statuses_to_lap,
                                       burn_per_lap_kg=<resolved rate>)
                where ``all_statuses_to_lap`` is the full sequence of
                track_status strings for laps 1..lap_nums[i] from lap_times
                (indexed 0 = lap 1). NEVER computed with track_statuses=None.
                The burn rate is resolved once per (year, gp) via
                ``fuel_features.resolve_race_burn_rate`` (#575 g4): the
                calibrated per-(season, circuit) dry rate from
                session_fuel_features, or mass_model's DEFAULT_BURN_PER_LAP_KG
                when the DB is unpopulated (a no-op vs. prior defaults).
burn_rate_source : Provenance of the resolved burn rate: 'session' | 'season_mean'
                | 'global_default' (fuel_features.resolve_race_burn_rate) or
                'not_applicable' for Q/SQ sessions.
cumulative_track_laps : Count of all driver-laps in lap_times for this session
                where lap_number < this stint's first clean lap.
                This is W3's track-evolution axis: how much rubber has been
                laid down before this stint began.
rho           : Session air density (kg/m^3). From measured FastF1 weather
                data (Pressure × 100 Pa, AirTemp °C, Humidity %) if available;
                falls back to 1.225 kg/m^3 (ISA sea level).
n_race_laps   : Total race laps: max(lap_number) across ALL drivers in session.
n_clean_laps  : Count of clean laps in this stint.
tyre_life_start : tyre_life at the first clean lap (documentation/indexing aid).
tyre_life_end   : tyre_life at the last clean lap (documentation/indexing aid).
sparse        : True when n_clean_laps < 5 (short stint / DNF / injury).

name: _ro_uri
doc: Convert an absolute DB path to a SQLite read-only URI.

name: _get_session_id
doc: Return session_id for the given session type, or None if not found.

name: _load_driver_laps
doc:
Load ALL lap_times rows for this driver in this session (ordered by lap_number).

Columns: lap_number, compound, tyre_life, stint_id, track_status,
         valid_lap, pit_in_time, pit_out_time

name: _get_n_race_laps
doc: Return max(lap_number) across ALL drivers in the session.

name: compute_cumulative_track_laps
doc:
Count total field laps completed before this stint's first clean lap.

Counts ALL driver-laps in ``lap_times`` for this session where
``lap_number < first_clean_lap_num``, regardless of ``valid_lap`` or
``track_status``.  This is the W3 track-evolution axis: total rubber laid
down before this stint started.

Parameters
----------
session_id           : Session ID in the SQLite DB.
first_clean_lap_num  : Race lap number of the first clean lap in the stint.
db_path              : Absolute path to the season SQLite DB.

Returns
-------
int : Count of (driver, lap) pairs with lap_number < first_clean_lap_num.

name: _constructor_drivers
doc:
Driver abbreviations racing for ``constructor`` in this weekend's session.

Resolved from ``session_classifications.team`` -- ``lap_times`` itself carries no
constructor/team column, so this is the seam. Best-effort: returns ``[]`` (never
raises) when the table, the weekend, or the constructor is absent.

name: _fastest_clean_lap_number
doc:
``lap_number`` of the fastest ``valid_lap=1`` lap among ``drivers`` in this session.

Returns ``None`` when ``drivers`` is empty or none of them has a clean lap.

name: session_cumulative_track_laps
doc:
Rubber-at-representative-lap for ``constructor`` in this session (#513 G3 unlock).

Anchors at the constructor's fastest clean (``valid_lap=1``) lap in this session --
its pace-representative lap, resolved via ``_constructor_drivers`` (constructor ->
driver_ids, from ``session_classifications.team``) and ``_fastest_clean_lap_number``
(the fastest of those drivers' clean laps) -- then reuses
:func:`compute_cumulative_track_laps` UNCHANGED to count total FIELD laps (every car,
not just this constructor's own) run before that lap's ``lap_number``. This is the same
"lap_number < anchor" convention :class:`RaceStintData` uses on the race side, so the
two stay on one comparable scale.

APPROXIMATION (stated explicitly, not silently assumed away): the downstream estimator
(``session_estimator``) pools observations across MANY laps at varying track states
within a session. Collapsing that to a single scalar per (session, constructor),
anchored at one representative lap, is a deliberate simplification for a first unlock --
it is not a claim that track evolution is uniform across every lap the estimator
actually used.

Returns ``None`` (never raises) when: the session is not found; the constructor has no
driver rows in ``session_classifications`` for this weekend; or none of those drivers
has a clean lap in this session.

name: _session_rho
doc: Extract air density from session weather; fall back to ISA sea-level.

name: _is_clean
doc: True if this lap row is a qualifying (clean) lap for physics fitting.

name: _calibrate_driver_hp
doc:
Calibrate smoother HP for a driver; return ``(hp, driver_tele_laps)``.

Returns ``(None, None)`` when there are no usable calibration windows or the
calibration raises (the raise is logged, matching the original inline block).

Calibrate HP on the biggest continuous span we can get for this driver.
For race sessions the smoother HP calibration needs to avoid pit-lane
dynamics (#538): we use the flying-lap windows (clean laps) as the
calibration windows.

``hp_store``/``session_key`` are the opt-in persistence cache (Task 14) —
forwarded straight through to ``calibrate_session_hp``; either omitted
(the default) is byte-identical to pre-Task-14 behaviour.

name: _median_hp
doc:
Field-wise median across a pool of calibrated HPs.

``order`` is taken from the first entry (all native calibrations in this
codebase run at a fixed order, so the pool is homogeneous); ``nu`` medians
over only the non-None entries (falls back to None if every entry lacks it).

name: _pooled_session_hp
doc:
Median HP across up to ``_POOL_MAX_CANDIDATES`` OTHER drivers who
calibrate natively in this SAME (already-loaded) session.

Reuses the session object the caller already has -- no extra TelemetryStore
read. Returns None if no other driver in the session calibrates either.

name: _cached_pooled_hp
doc:
Cache wrapper for :func:`_pooled_session_hp`, keyed per (year, gp,
session_type) so a session with many failing drivers only pays for the
pool scan once. Safe to share across different ``exclude_driver`` values:
any driver reaching this tier has already failed its own native
calibration, so it was never a viable pool candidate regardless of which
caller's exclusion first populated the cache.

name: _borrow_hp_from_session
doc:
Attempt native-style HP calibration for ``driver`` in a DIFFERENT
session of the same weekend. Returns None on any absence/failure (missing
session, driver not entered, insufficient telemetry, or calibration
itself failing) -- borrowing is best-effort, never fatal to the caller.

name: _cached_borrow
doc: Cache wrapper for :func:`_borrow_hp_from_session`.

name: _hp_fallback
doc:
Recover a usable SmootherHP when native (own-session) calibration fails.

Only called for non-R session types (the caller gates on session_type; see
_fit_driver_laps). Tries, in priority order: (1) the same driver's RACE
session HP, (2) the same driver's HP from another practice session, (3) the
pooled median HP of other drivers who calibrated natively in THIS session.

Returns ``(hp, driver_tele_laps, source)``. ``driver_tele_laps`` is always
drawn from THIS (native) session -- lap numbers in the per-lap fit loop
refer to this session, so a borrowed HP must never be paired with a
borrowed session's lap-timing table. Returns ``(None, None, None)`` when
every fallback tier fails (caller drops the driver, same as before this
fallback existed).

name: _score_and_persist_pvat
doc:
Score this fitted lap's trust profile, log it, and persist to PVAT
unless gated out (#3, trust-profile wiring; split out of
``_fit_clean_lap_row`` to keep that function's length in bounds).

Always computes ``grading.compute_trust_profile`` over the SAME padded
window ``fit_lap`` fit ``ss`` on (``info["tp"/"yX"/"yY"/"tc"/"yV"]``, the
same object being persisted) and logs it -- log-only signal, the
default. When ``max_trust_chi2`` is given, a lap whose held-out chi^2
(position OR speed stream) exceeds it has its PVAT write SKIPPED
(logged, not fatal) -- gating affects persistence only, never the
caller's in-memory fit result.

COST: ``compute_trust_profile``'s held-out chi^2 runs one extra
``StintSmoother`` refit over this same lap+overhang window (on top of
the 3 refits ``fit_lap``'s own ``n_boot=2`` bootstrap already pays) --
roughly +33% per LAP, only ever paid on this (already opt-in) pvat_db
path, never per-session.

FAIL-OPEN: a trust-profile computation failure (any exception) is
logged and treated as "no gate, no scalars" -- ``max_trust_chi2`` does
NOT gate that lap, the write proceeds normally, and the four
``trust_*`` columns are written as NULL. Scoring a fit must never be
able to block persisting it.

name: _fit_clean_lap_row
doc:
Fit one clean lap; return ``(lap_number, processed_df)`` or ``None`` to skip.

Mutates ``stint_bounds`` in place (caches per-stint overhang clamps).

``pvat_db`` is the opt-in PVAT persistence hook (Task 10): when not
``None``, the fitted lap's smoother output is also written to
``processed_telemetry`` via ``write_lap_pvat`` (keyed by ``year``/``gp``/
``session_type``/``driver``/lap number) -- see
``_score_and_persist_pvat`` for the trust-profile scoring/gating this
also runs (#3). Defaults to ``None`` -- the default path writes zero
rows and never scores a trust profile.

name: _fit_driver_laps
doc:
Fit each clean lap via trajectory smoother. Returns {lap_number: processed_df}.

Calibrates smoother HP once per driver-session on a representative stint/window,
then fits each clean lap independently with ``fit_lap``.  Per-lap failures are
skipped (not fatal — the stint is still returned; n_clean_laps drops).

The session object must expose the DBSession interface (pos_data/car_data keyed
by driver number string, get_driver, laps.pick_drivers).

``year``/``gp``/``store_path`` are only used for the non-R HP fallback (see
``_hp_fallback``); ``session_type='R'`` NEVER engages the fallback -- when
native calibration fails on the race path this function returns {} exactly
as it always has. ``year``/``gp``/``session_type`` are ALSO threaded down to
``_fit_clean_lap_row`` as the PVAT persistence keys (Task 10) regardless of
session type; ``pvat_db`` (default ``None``, opt-in) is passed through
unchanged -- see ``_fit_clean_lap_row``'s docstring.

``hp_store`` (opt-in, Task 14) is the smoother-HP calibration cache -- forwarded to
the NATIVE ``_calibrate_driver_hp`` call only (below), keyed on ``(year, gp,
session_type, driver)`` when ``year``/``gp`` are given. The non-R fallback tiers
(``_hp_fallback`` -> ``_pooled_session_hp``/``_borrow_hp_from_session``) are
untouched by this wiring and never populate or read ``hp_store``.

``max_trust_chi2`` (opt-in, #3) is forwarded straight through to
``_fit_clean_lap_row`` -- see its docstring. Defaults to ``None`` (no
gating).

name: _lap_masses
doc:
Per-lap car mass for a session.

Q/SQ: constant quali trim (short low-fuel runs; no burn model).
R/S : race_mass with the session's own lap count — for a sprint this
      yields the sprint-scale start fuel (burn x distance, ~30-40 kg).

``statuses_by_lap[i]`` is the per-lap track_status prefix (laps 1..lap_num)
for ``lap_nums[i]`` — race_mass/fuel_at_lap never receives
``track_statuses=None`` for R/S (the module's hard gate).

name: _build_track_statuses
doc:
Build a complete per-lap track_status vector (index 0 = lap 1).

Maps lap_number -> track_status from lap_times, filling missing laps with
"1" so ``race_mass`` always receives real statuses (never None).

name: _group_clean_stints
doc:
Filter to clean laps and group them by stint_id (each reset-index'd).

Returns ``(clean_df, stints_grouped)``; ``stints_grouped`` is empty when
there are no clean laps. Coerces None/NaN pit times to Python None (in
place) to match the clean-lap gate.

name: _build_race_stint
doc:
Build one :class:`RaceStintData` for a stint, or None when it is dropped.

Dropped when the stint has fewer than ``min_clean_laps`` clean laps.

name: _prepare_fitted_laps
doc:
Load the TelemetryStore session, derive rho, and fit all clean laps.

Returns ``(rho, fitted_laps)``. rho falls back to ISA sea-level when there is
no stored session. Per-driver smoother fitting failures are logged and yield
an empty fitted-laps dict (non-fatal).

``pvat_db`` (default ``None``) is the opt-in PVAT persistence hook (Task
10), passed straight through to ``_fit_driver_laps``. ``hp_store`` (default
``None``) is the opt-in smoother-HP calibration cache (Task 14), likewise
passed straight through. ``max_trust_chi2`` (default ``None``, opt-in #3)
is likewise forwarded unchanged.

name: load_race_stints
doc:
Load race stints for one driver, returning one :class:`RaceStintData` per stint.

Parameters
----------
year          : Championship year.
gp            : GP name as stored in the SQLite ``sessions`` table.
driver        : Driver abbreviation (e.g. 'VER').
db_path       : Absolute path to the season SQLite DB (e.g. 'data/f1_data_2023.db').
store_path    : Optional path to the TelemetryStore DB. Defaults to
                ``DEFAULT_STORE_PATH`` from ``src.data.telemetry_store``.
min_clean_laps: Minimum clean laps to include a stint (default 1).
                Stints with fewer clean laps after filtering are dropped entirely.
session_type  : Session type to load: ``'R'`` (race, default), ``'S'``
                (sprint), ``'Q'``, ``'SQ'``. Q/SQ use a constant
                quali-trim mass instead of the race burn-down model.
pvat_db       : Opt-in PVAT persistence hook (Task 10). Defaults to
                ``None`` -- the default path writes zero rows. When a
                ``DatabaseManager`` is supplied, this driver's prior
                ``processed_telemetry`` rows for this session are deleted
                first (``pvat_writer.ensure_clean_pvat``), then every
                fitted clean lap's smoother output is persisted via
                ``src.physics.ideal_lap.pvat_writer.write_lap_pvat`` --
                re-running or resuming an export is idempotent (row
                count is identical to a single run), not additive.
hp_store      : Opt-in smoother-HP calibration cache (Task 14). Defaults to
                ``None`` -- calibrate_session_hp's chi^2-target search always
                re-runs, exactly as before this seam existed. When an
                ``HPStore`` is supplied, the NATIVE (own-session)
                calibration for (year, gp, session_type, driver) is looked
                up first and stored on a miss; the non-R HP-fallback tiers
                (``_hp_fallback``) are untouched by this cache. NOTE: a
                cached row's ``code_version`` is provenance-only -- it does
                NOT invalidate a cache hit. Only a manual ``_SCHEME_VERSION``
                bump in ``hp_store.py`` (or a change to calibration order /
                the flying-window-union flag) invalidates old rows.
max_trust_chi2: Opt-in PVAT quality gate (#3). Defaults to ``None`` --
                log-only: whenever ``pvat_db`` is active, every fitted
                lap's trust profile (held-out chi^2 + NIS summary,
                ``grading.compute_trust_profile``) is always computed and
                logged, but every lap is still persisted. When given, a
                lap whose held-out chi^2 (either stream) exceeds this
                value has its PVAT write skipped -- the lap itself is
                unaffected (still returned in this call's
                ``RaceStintData``), only its persistence to
                ``processed_telemetry`` is gated. Has no effect when
                ``pvat_db`` is ``None``.
                COST: computing the trust profile (whenever ``pvat_db``
                is active, regardless of whether ``max_trust_chi2`` is
                set) runs one extra held-out ``StintSmoother`` refit over
                the same lap+overhang window ``fit_lap`` already fit --
                roughly +33% on top of a lap's existing 3-refit
                bootstrap cost (``_fit_nonstationary_core``'s
                ``n_boot=2``), i.e. per-LAP, not per-session. This is why
                the gate is opt-in on the already-opt-in ``pvat_db``
                path rather than always-on.
                FAIL-OPEN: a ``compute_trust_profile`` exception (bad
                inputs, numerical failure, anything) is caught and
                logged; the lap is treated as having no trust profile,
                ``max_trust_chi2`` does NOT gate it (the write proceeds
                normally), and the four ``trust_*`` columns are written
                as NULL for that lap. Scoring a fit can never block
                persisting it.

Returns
-------
list[RaceStintData] — one entry per qualifying stint (ordered by stint_num).
Empty list if the driver has no clean laps or the session is not found.

Raises
------
Does not raise for missing sessions/drivers — returns [].
Raises for misconfigured DB path (sqlite3.DatabaseError) or store path issues.

name: PhysicsEstimatorConfig
doc:
Configuration parameters for physics-based parameter estimation.

This config controls all aspects of the estimation pipeline including:
- Control signal interpolation (kernel bandwidth)
- Segment classification thresholds
- Longitudinal dynamics fitting
- Lateral envelope fitting
- Atmospheric conditions

All parameters have sensible defaults for F1 telemetry data at ~50ms sample rate.

name: __post_init__
doc: Validate configuration parameters after initialization.

name: _validate_positive
doc: Validate that a value is strictly positive.

name: _validate_non_negative
doc: Validate that a value is non-negative.

name: _validate_unit_range
doc: Validate that a value is in the open interval (0, 1).

name: _validate_positive_int
doc: Validate that a value is a positive integer.

name: from_config
doc:
Build PhysicsEstimatorConfig from the YAML configuration file.

Falls back to dataclass defaults if no physics section exists.

name: _engine_sha
doc: Short git SHA of the engine producing a fit (best-effort, cached once).

name: _now_iso
doc: UTC timestamp for when a fit was produced (run provenance).

name: _power_curve
doc:
Serialize LongitudinalParameters' theta_P trio for ``FitRecord.power_curve``.

Mirrors ``specific_power_times_s`` / ``specific_power_w_kg`` /
``specific_power_covariance`` 1:1 (native units, W/kg = m^2/s^3) -- see
``fit_store.FitRecord.power_curve``. Both arrays are always populated
(``LongitudinalParameters.__post_init__`` coerces them, and
``ParameterEstimator._build_longitudinal`` has a single-point fallback),
so this always returns a dict, never ``None``.

name: record_from_params
doc: Flatten a PhysicsParameterSet (+ envelope flags + apex obs) to a FitRecord.

name: _density_from_session
doc:
Per-session air density from a loaded session's weather stream.

Returns ``(rho_kg_m3, rho_is_fallback)``.  ``rho_is_fallback`` is ``True``
when real weather data was unavailable and ``DEFAULT_RHO`` was substituted.
Operates on the in-memory ``session.weather_data`` of an already-loaded
session — it reads no cache and imports no ``fastf1``.

name: load_quali_session
doc:
Load a quali session with weather; return (session, rho, rho_is_fallback).

Source order (#494): the durable telemetry SQLite store first, the FastF1
cache as fallback.  When ``data/telemetry_store.db`` (or ``store``) holds the
requested session, a DB-backed session shim is returned and the fit chain
rebuilds from the DB rather than the volatile cache.  Otherwise loading is
routed through the single preprocessing cache seam
(``preprocessing.trajectory.loaders.load_session``) so the physics region
never imports ``fastf1`` or touches the FastF1 cache directly (#503).

Either way the returned session quacks like a FastF1 session over the surface
the fit chain consumes, and air density is derived from the session's
in-memory weather stream.  The third return value is ``True`` when real
weather data was unavailable and ``DEFAULT_RHO`` was substituted.

Parameters
----------
store : str | None
    Optional path to the telemetry store DB; ``None`` uses the canonical
    ``data/telemetry_store.db``.  A missing store transparently falls back to
    the cache.

name: _build_control_df
doc: control_df (throttle/brake/gear/drs) for one lap window. Lifted from diagnostics.

name: _calibrate_hp_for_driver
doc:
Calibrate smoother HPs on a driver's fastest stint + flying-lap windows.

Shared by ``fit_driver`` and ``fit_session_full`` — identical logic. Builds
flying-lap windows for HP calibration (excludes in/out-lap #538).

``hp_store``/``session_key`` are the opt-in persistence cache (Task 14) —
forwarded straight through to ``calibrate_session_hp``; either omitted
(the default) is byte-identical to pre-Task-14 behaviour.

name: _fit_flying_laps
doc:
Fit each flying lap → processed telemetry + control_df, capturing the best lap.

Shared by ``fit_driver`` and ``fit_session_full``. Returns
``(proc, ctrl, best_df)`` where ``best_df`` is the processed telemetry of the
fastest lap (``None`` if it was skipped). ``skip_msg`` is the debug-log format
string for a skipped lap (caller-specific to preserve existing log text).

name: fit_driver
doc: Run the lifted production chain for one driver on a preloaded session.

name: SessionFitFull
doc:
Result of a full re-fit for the two-sided ideal-lap diagnostic (P1).

Contains the fitted PhysicsParameterSet (including the power curve needed
by the simulator) and the best lap's arc-length distance array and
smoothed speed array — both sampled at the smoother's native resolution.

Attributes
----------
params:
    Fitted ``PhysicsParameterSet`` (all sub-parameter sets populated).
best_distance:
    Cumulative arc-length of the best lap (m), shape (N,).
    Computed as ``np.cumsum(np.hypot(np.diff(px), np.diff(py)))`` with a
    leading 0.  Suitable as the ``xp`` argument to ``np.interp``.
best_speed_real:
    Smoothed speed trace of the best lap (m/s), shape (N,).
best_lap_s:
    Best-lap time (s) as reported by FastF1.

name: fit_session_full
doc:
Re-fit one driver on a preloaded session and return params + best-lap geometry.

This is the diagnostic entry point for ``sim_evaluator.evaluate_session``.
It reproduces the same smoother→adapter→estimator chain as ``fit_driver``
(DRY: shared imports, same pooling logic) but ALSO captures the best lap's
``px``, ``py``, ``speed_ms`` columns so the caller can align sim vs. real.

Parameters
----------
session:
    Preloaded FastF1 session (``s.load(telemetry=True, laps=True, weather=True)``).
driver:
    Driver abbreviation (e.g. ``"VER"``).
year:
    Season year (for regulation era selection).
gp_name:
    GP name (for logging).
rho:
    Air density (kg/m³) at which the session was run.
cfg:
    Optional ``PhysicsEstimatorConfig`` override.

Returns
-------
``SessionFitFull`` on success; ``None`` when no valid flying laps exist.

name: fit_best_lap_trace
doc:
Re-derive ONLY the real best lap's smoothed distance/speed trace.

A cheap subset of ``fit_session_full``'s chain, for ``sim_evaluator``'s
store-hit path (#575 follow-on, sim-evaluator wiring): once ``params``
itself is reconstructed from a ``FitStore`` row
(``fit_store.params_from_record``), the only thing left to recover is the
real best-lap trace the evaluator diffs the sim against — ``FitStore``
never persists it (only the scalar ``best_lap_s``). This runs HP
calibration on the SAME inputs/windows ``fit_session_full`` would use (so
a byte-identical HP), then a SINGLE ``fit_lap`` call on the fastest lap
only — skipping every other flying lap's smoothing AND
``ParameterEstimator.estimate_parameters`` entirely (the single most
expensive step). ``hp_store``/``session_key`` forward straight through to
``calibrate_session_hp`` (Task 14's opt-in cache), so a warm cache costs
exactly one ``fit_lap`` call.

Returns ``(best_distance, best_speed_real, best_lap_s)`` on success — the
same values ``fit_session_full`` would have captured for the fastest lap
— or ``None`` when the fastest lap itself can't be smoothed (the caller
should fall back to the full re-fit path in that case, same as any other
store-hit miss).

name: _is_concentrated
doc:
Two independent fragility triggers, either one flags the cell (not
excludes it): (a) ``n_corners<=1`` -- a pooled kappa backed by a single
corner has no cross-corner corroboration; (b)
``n_stints<=CONCENTRATED_MIN_STINTS`` -- the LODO stint-concentration
concern (see the module-level comment above ``CONCENTRATED_MIN_STINTS``)
-- a cell resting on few stints is fragile to one driver's idiosyncrasy
even when several corners agree.

name: _git_sha
doc:
Short git commit hash, or "unknown" when git is unavailable/fails --
tests must not require a git checkout.

name: _year_gps
doc: GPs fingerprint_year actually produced rows for (empty -> []).

name: _sweep_missing
doc:
Sweep any (year, gp) lacking a per-event laps CSV (``--sweep-missing``
only). Reuses an existing windows CSV when present (window reuse).

name: _cell_quality
doc:
Per-(gp, compound) n_corners/n_stints, from the SAME filtered panel
rows ``season_model.load_year_axis`` pools over (EXCLUDE + flat-out +
traction_only) -- duplicated here because ``load_year_axis`` only
returns the pooled kappa/se, not the per-corner detail the wear_cells
data-quality columns need. n_corners = number of distinct corners whose
fit contributed to this (gp, compound)'s pooled kappa; n_stints = the
largest per-corner stint count among them (the same physical stints are
reused across a race's corners, so max is the race's real stint count,
not a sum that would double-count).

name: _axis_cells
doc:
One axis's wear_cells rows across ``years``: load_year_axis's pooled
kappa/se, joined to rubber_map's cnum (rows without a yaml allocation are
dropped -- fit_axis requires an int cnum) and is_wet's wet flag, plus the
_cell_quality data-quality columns. Empty (matching CELLS_COLUMNS) if no
year has a panel CSV for this axis's phase.

name: _pool_mass_beta
doc:
Task 5b: pool Task 3's per-corner ``kappa_mass_pct`` into ONE shared
additive mass-wear beta per axis, inverse-variance weighted across
EVERY corner/circuit/year this batch run covers (matching the pooled
~0.031 %/lap-per-100kg finding, ``scripts/mass_wear_probe.py``'s Cut
1b) -- one number per axis for the WHOLE run, not per year (mass is a
physical constant, not a per-season quantity the way rubber R is).

Returns ``{axis_abbr: (beta, se)}``; an axis absent from the dict
means no corner in this batch identified a mass term at all
(``mass_beta`` wasn't turned on for this run, or every corner's fit was
too thin/missing the column) -- the caller must not write a fabricated
``wear_factors`` row for it. A non-finite pooled result is treated the
same as "absent": the writer must never emit NaN.

name: _massbeta_kappa_corr_pool
doc:
Task 7: pool the per-corner beta_mass x beta_c covariance (panel's
``kappa_{c}_massbeta_cov``, populated only when a corner's panel fit
ran with ``mass_beta=True``) into ONE Fisher-z-pooled correlation per
axis for the WHOLE run -- same "one number per axis for the whole run"
posture as ``_pool_mass_beta``.

Each (corner, compound) cell with a populated ``kappa_{c}_massbeta_cov``
contributes one correlation sample ``r = cov / (beta_mass_se *
d_{c}_se)`` (both SEs already on the panel CSV -- no new column
needed). Correlations are not safely averaged directly (``r``'s
sampling distribution is skewed near +-1); the Fisher z-transform
(``arctanh``) stabilizes the variance first, the mean is taken in
z-space, then ``tanh`` inverse-transforms the pooled mean back to a
correlation.

Returns ``{}`` for an axis with no such sample at all (mass_beta off
for this run, or every corner's fit too thin to have both a beta_mass
and a beta_c SE) -- the caller must not write a fabricated value for
it. A non-finite pooled result is treated the same as absent, mirroring
``_pool_mass_beta``'s own guard.

name: _factors_and_cov
doc:
fit_axis's {S, R, cov} -> (wear_factors rows, wear_cov rows) for one
axis. Factor se is the sqrt of that key's cov diagonal entry; the
gauge-fixed reference R key has no cov entry (see factor_covariance's
docstring) so its se is None.

name: run_batch
doc:
Run the canonical batch path and write a new versioned run. Returns
the new run_id.

``coast``/``push_quantile`` (Task 4, capability-wear-model-v2, default
``coast=None`` -> byte-identical to the pre-Task-4 batch): threaded
straight to both ``panel_year`` calls, which merge it in per gp and fit
the push-conditioned capability kappa alongside the unchanged realized
one (see ``panel.fit_panel``'s docstring). No further wiring is needed
downstream -- ``season_model.load_year_axis`` pools whichever
``kappa_cap_{c}`` columns land in the panel CSVs (present only when
``coast`` was supplied) into ``kappa_cap``/``se_cap``, and
``_axis_cells`` carries those columns straight through to
``store.CELLS_COLUMNS`` unchanged.

``coast`` accepts either shape:

- A year-keyed ``dict[int, pd.DataFrame]`` (``_load_coast_tables``'s
  shape, preferred): each year's own coast table
  (``coast.get(year)``, possibly missing/None) is threaded to that
  year's ``panel_year`` calls ONLY. This is the fix for a real
  cross-year data-contamination bug (found during the run-5 rebuild
  investigation): the old single-DataFrame path applied the SAME
  concatenated table to every year, and ``panel.py`` narrows a coast
  table by gp only, then ``_capability_fit`` merges on (driver, lap)
  after ``drop_duplicates(subset=["driver", "lap"])`` -- so a (gp,
  driver, lap) key recurring across years (Abu Dhabi 2019 vs. 2020
  measured 867/~1000 colliding pairs) silently let the EARLIEST year
  in the batch's coast table win every later year's push-lap split.
  Runs before this fix (run_id<=4 in the production db) carry that
  contamination in their capability kappa; run 5+ is clean.
- A single ``pd.DataFrame`` (legacy/back-compat, still needed by the
  single-year test fixtures): applied identically to every year in
  ``years``, i.e. the OLD contaminated semantics. Fine when ``years``
  really is one year; a multi-year batch given a single DataFrame logs
  a loud warning (the same collision risk above) but still runs (no
  behavior change for existing single-DataFrame callers).

``mass_beta`` (Task 5b, capability-wear-model-v2, default ``True``):
threaded to both ``panel_year`` calls so every corner's panel fit also
estimates the shared age x mass_dev term (Task 3), then pooled across
every corner/circuit/year in this run (``_pool_mass_beta``, IVW) into
ONE additive beta per axis and written as a ``wear_factors`` row
(``kind="mass_beta"``). Defaults to ``True`` (unconditional, NOT gated
on ``coast`` being supplied): mass-wear is a separate, orthogonal
physical term from the realized-vs-capability push split -- it costs
nothing extra to estimate (``panel_year`` derives the per-lap mass
itself via ``mass_model.race_mass``, no external data needed) and
gating it on coast availability would arbitrarily deprive a
coast-less run of a term we can always compute. This is NOT
byte-identical to the pre-Task-5b batch by construction (that is the
point of this task -- a real batch run should ship the mass_beta row);
set ``False`` to reproduce the pre-Task-5b/pre-Task-3-wiring batch
output exactly (no ``age_mass`` design column, no mass_beta row).

name: _load_coast_tables
doc:
Auto-load per-year ``coast_frac_{year}.csv`` tables (Task 1's
``push_signal.write_coast_table`` output) for the CLI capability path
(Task 4 review Q2) -- WITHOUT generating them (that's a separate data
run, not this CLI's job).

Returns a year-keyed ``{year: df}`` mapping (fix for the cross-year
(gp, driver, lap) collision bug -- see ``run_batch``'s docstring): a
year missing its CSV just contributes no key (logged, not a crash;
that year's panel fits run coast-less for it). Returns None
(realized-only, byte-identical to the pre-Task-4/pre-coast batch) only
if NONE of ``years`` has a coast table on disk.

name: DensityFit
doc:
Within-car-season fixed-effects OLS slope of one axis on ln(rho).

``beta`` / ``se`` are always the empirical fit (diagnostic, for audit),
regardless of whether the axis is actually applied. ``applied`` says
whether ``apply_layer1`` uses this beta (True) or forces the explained
density component to 0 for this axis (False, an honest physical null).

name: fit_density_betas
doc:
Fit each axis's within-car-season OLS slope on ln(rho).

Demeans both the axis value and ln(rho) by their car-season means (a
fixed-effects regression), so the slope reflects density leakage AFTER
removing each car's own average level -- not raw cross-circuit
performance differences. Only car-seasons with >= ``min_weekends`` ok
rows contribute (their own-mean is trustworthy). Returns one
:class:`DensityFit` per axis; ``applied`` is set from
``DENSITY_SENSITIVE_AXES`` (the empirical ``beta``/``se`` are still
computed and returned for every axis as a diagnostic).

name: apply_layer1
doc:
Add ``{axis}_explained`` / ``{axis}_residual`` / ``{axis}_layer1_sigma`` per axis.

``density_fits`` defaults to a fresh :func:`fit_density_betas` call over
``df``. ``mass_kg_assumed``'s reference is this ``df``'s own mean (no
module-level DB-derived constant -- the reference is a function of the
data passed in, per project doctrine on mutable/derived state).

name: mexico_monaco_residual_consistency
doc:
Per shared (year, constructor) Mexico<->Monaco raw and residual gaps.

Returns one row per car-season present at BOTH venues with:
``raw_gap`` (Mexico axis - Monaco axis, i.e. density completely ignored),
``resid_gap`` (Mexico residual - Monaco residual, i.e. after Layer 1),
``sigma`` (combined propagated sigma for the residual gap), and the
corresponding |z| = |gap| / sigma for both. See module docstring for the
honest setup-confound caveat this comparison is subject to.
